claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information!

Since Alex is 19 years old, they're over 16, so I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

(Approved education includes A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications – but not university degrees or other higher education. Approved training means unpaid training courses that aren't part of a job contract.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that Alex is studying for A-levels at sixth form college. That counts as approved education, which is good news for eligibility.

Just a couple more questions:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful.

Now I just need to confirm a few more details about your situation with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or do you contribute towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to complete the eligibility check:

**Does Alex work 24 hours or more per week in paid employment, or receive any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he does have a job - he works full-time at the supermarket. But he's still doing his A-levels at the same time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important detail. I just need to clarify:

**When you say Alex works "full-time," does that mean he works 24 hours or more per week?**

This is important because working 24 hours or more per week while in education can affect Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he works more than 24 hours a week - it's a proper full-time job alongside his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Unfortunately, I have to share some news that may be disappointing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Here's why:

While Alex meets several of the usual criteria:
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you
- ✅ Alex is under 20 and in approved education (A-levels)

Unfortunately, there's one condition that affects eligibility:
- ❌ **Alex works 24 hours or more per week in paid employment**

The rules state that Child Benefit stops if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week, even if they remain in approved education or training.

### What you could consider:

If Alex's working hours were to reduce to below 24 hours per week while he continues his A-level studies, you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit again. If his circumstances change, you're welcome to check your eligibility at that time.

I hope this information is helpful. Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?

While Alex is still in approved education, he is also working more than 24 hours per week in paid employment. According to the rules, working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment means Child Benefit eligibility stops, even if the child is still in education. Therefore, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
